title: Enhanced structured-response contract for progressive streaming + tool integration
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Define a developer-facing contract that governs structured responses emitted by models when invoking external tools (function calls), with special focus on progressive/streaming output, explicit error frames, and schema reconciliation for post-processing and rerouting. This PRD clarifies scope, acceptance criteria, test scenarios, rollout constraints, and telemetry needed for a safe rollout across hosted and dedicated modes.
background: Existing tickets cover streaming JSON, function-call acceptance, and basic fallback behaviors. Customers have requested stronger guarantees when outputs are streamed and when a response must trigger a tool call: fewer silent failures, clear marker frames for tool invocation, and post-stream schema validation hooks so downstream runtimes can decide retry vs fallback. We need a single concise contract that operations, SDKs, and the runtime can implement consistently.
goals: Specify a compact envelope format for progressive streaming that includes metadata frames (init, tool-invoke, partial-schema, error, final) and is backward compatible with simple text streams
Define deterministic behavior for function/tool invocation when invoked mid-stream: when to pause, ACK semantics, and how the runtime should surface transient schema drift
List acceptance tests and observable signals (telemetry) that determine pass/fail for rollout gating
Surface non-functional constraints: max latency for tool-ACK, bounded number of partial-schema updates, and graceful degrade paths for SDKs that don't implement streaming envelopes
non_goals: Specifying language-level serialization libraries for every SDK (we will publish reference implementations only)
Fundamental change to existing model prompting heuristics (this ticket defines an output contract only)
Extending the contract to binary streaming or embedding payloads in this phase
acceptance_criteria: Envelope frames: runtime emits and SDKs accept the following top-level frames: INIT (stream metadata), PARTIAL (incremental structured chunk), TOOL_CALL (tool id + args marker), ERROR (error code + human message), END (final schema-complete marker)
Backward compatibility: if an SDK receives plain text without envelope markers, it must treat the stream as legacy text-mode and continue to surface tokens unchanged

Mid-stream tool-calls: when a TOOL_CALL frame is emitted mid-stream the runtime must pause the token emission, surface a TOOL_PENDING telemetry event, and deliver a TOOL_ACK requirement to the runner within 500ms; if ACK not returned within 2s the runtime must emit ERROR(code=TOOL_TIMEOUT) then either continue with fallback text or close stream based on route policy

Partial-schema updates: PARTIAL frames may include a partial JSON schema; the runtime guarantees at most 3 schema evolution frames per stream and each must be monotonic (fields added or narrowed; no removal of previously declared required fields)

Robust validation: at END frame the runtime must validate final assembled payload against the last declared schema; if mismatch, emit ERROR(code=SCHEMA_MISMATCH) and mark response as invalid in telemetry with a pointer to first invalid field

Tool-safety: when TOOL_CALL is declared with a tool id not present in the allowed-toolset for the API key, the runtime must emit ERROR(code=UNAUTHORIZED_TOOL) and prevent invocation; SDKs must surface this error clearly to callers

Streaming fallback: if a client indicates non-streaming-only capability in handshake, runtime may buffer and deliver assembled final payload as a single response but must still enforce schema validation and error semantics

SDK reference behavior: reference JS and Python SDKs must implement parsing of envelope frames and provide a convenience event API: onInit, onPartial, onToolCall, onError, onEnd. Both SDKs must be able to deliver assembled structured payload to downstream code even when content was streamed
End-to-end tests: minimum 12 automated scenarios pass in CI covering legacy text stream, envelope streaming happy-path, tool-timeout, schema-evolution, unauthorized-tool, and schema-mismatch aborts
test_scenarios: Happy-path streaming structured output that declares schema in INIT, emits PARTIAL chunks, TOOL_CALL with valid tool id, receives TOOL_ACK within 100ms, and ends with valid payload — assert assembled JSON matches schema
Tool timeout: MODEL emits TOOL_CALL but runner does not ACK within 2s — assert ERROR(TOOL_TIMEOUT) emitted, telemetry TOOL_PENDING recorded, and stream fallback behavior chosen per route policy
Unauthorized tool: TOOL_CALL is emitted for disallowed tool id — assert no invocation, ERROR(UNAUTHORIZED_TOOL) returned, and SDK surfaces explicit exception
Schema drift detection: PARTIAL frames add a required field after earlier frames expected it optional — assert monotonicity violation triggers ERROR(SCHEMA_VIOLATION) and stream is marked invalid
Legacy client: client handshake indicates no envelope support and model emits envelope frames — assert SDK strips markers and returns raw tokens without breaking
Buffering mode: client requests non-streaming delivery but model generates envelope frames — runtime buffers and returns final assembled payload; assert schema validation still applied
Interleaved error: emit PARTIAL, then ERROR with recoverable flag — assert SDK calls onError but continues to accept subsequent PARTIAL frames when recoverable=true
Bandwidth edge: ensure large PARTIAL frames are chunked and reassembled correctly by SDK without losing order
rollout_requirements: Feature gated by runtime flag 'structured_streaming_v2' and must be opt-in for Dedicated customers during initial 6-week validation
Canary cohort: enable for 1% of hosted traffic with internal telemetry alerts on schema-mismatch >0.1% and tool-timeout >0.05% for automatic rollback
SDKs: publish JS/Python reference implementations and mark them experimental; require usage of reference SDK in 2 internal integration apps before broader rollout
Docs: publish protocol spec, error code list, and example integrations before enabling in >10% traffic
telemetry_requirements: Emit TOOL_PENDING, TOOL_ACK, TOOL_INVOKE, TOOL_INVOKE_RESULT, SCHEMA_UPDATE, SCHEMA_FINAL_VALIDATE, SCHEMA_MISMATCH, STREAM_LEGACY_FALLBACK events
Include route_id, client_capabilities (streaming/envelope), model_id, tool_id, elapsed_ms for ACK, number_of_schema_updates, and final_validation_status in each event
Create a dashboard that surfaces top 10 failing fields for SCHEMA_MISMATCH over last 7 days and a per-route heatmap for TOOL_TIMEOUTs
Define SLO alarm thresholds (default): SCHEMA_MISMATCH rate < 0.2% and TOOL_TIMEOUT rate < 0.1% per route
notes: Implementation work will require runtime support for pausing streams, an ACK/timeout subprotocol for tool calls, and SDK parsers. Engineering estimates indicate medium complexity due to interactions with batching and KV cache. We will coordinate with Security for tool allowlist checking and with Console for telemetry surfaces.
open_questions: Should a PARTIAL frame ever include binary blobs (e.g., base64 attachments) in this phase? (recommend: no)
What is the authoritative ordering guarantee for PARTIAL frames delivered during retries when network flaps occur? (recommend: runtime enforces monotonic sequence numbers)
Do we need an explicit developer-visible 'schema-rollback' mechanism to support graceful evolution across model versions?
How should long-running tool calls (>30s) be surfaced to downstream SDKs — keep connection open or provide a handle for polling?
